papers.title: Method of Manufactured Solutions Code Verification of Elastostatic Solid Mechanics Problems in a Commercial Finite Element Solver
papers.abstract: Much progress has been made in advancing and standardizing verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification practices for computational modeling in recent decades. However, examples of rigorous code verification for solid mechanics problems in the literature remain scarce, particularly for commercial software and for the non-trivial large-deformation analyses and nonlinear materials typically needed to simulate medical devices. Here, we apply the method of manufactured solutions (MMS) to verify a commercial finite element code for elastostatic solid mechanics analyses using linear-elastic, hyperelastic (neo-Hookean), and quasi-hyperelastic (Hencky) constitutive models. Analytical source terms are generated using either Python/SymPy or Mathematica and are implemented in ABAQUS/Standard without modification to the solver source code. Source terms for the three constitutive models are found to vary nearly six orders of magnitude in the number of mathematical operations they contain. Refinement studies reveal second-order displacement convergence in response to mesh refinement for all constitutive models and first-order displacement convergence in response to increment refinement for the finite-strain problems. We also investigate the sensitivity of MMS convergence order to minor coding errors using an exploratory case. Code used to generate the MMS source terms and the input files for the simulations are provided as supplemental material.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于有限元代码验证方法，未涉及代理模型、不确定性量化或生物力学设计优化。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on code verification of FEA solvers, not on surrogate modeling, uncertainty quantification, or optimization for implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 验证商业有限元软件在固体力学问题中的代码正确性。
summary_zh.method: 采用制造解方法生成解析源项，在ABAQUS中实现并测试线性弹性、超弹性等本构模型。
summary_zh.result: 所有本构模型均观察到二阶位移收敛，有限应变问题为一阶收敛。
summary_zh.validation: 通过网格细化研究验证收敛阶数，并测试编码错误敏感性。

summary_en.motivation: To rigorously verify the correctness of a commercial finite element code for elastostatic solid mechanics problems, which is essential for reliable medical device simulations.
summary_en.method: The method of manufactured solutions is applied to generate analytical source terms for linear-elastic, neo-Hookean, and Hencky constitutive models, implemented in ABAQUS/Standard without modifying the solver source code.
summary_en.result: Second-order displacement convergence is observed for all constitutive models under mesh refinement, while first-order convergence is found for finite-strain problems under increment refinement.
summary_en.validation: Convergence orders are verified through systematic mesh and increment refinement studies, with sensitivity analysis of coding errors.
